transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I’m here because... we recently put in a brighter mirror in our bathroom, and ever since then, I just keep noticing the skin around my cheeks and my jaw. It looks really uneven to me, or kind of saggy. My husband says he really can’t see what I’m talking about when I point it out, but it's just been bothering me enough that I wanted to come in and talk to someone.
How much has this concern about the skin on your cheeks and jaw been affecting your daily life or causing you distress?

Well, I still get my work done, so it hasn't stopped me from doing what I need to do. But... the extra time I spend getting ready in the morning has definitely made me rush into the courthouse a few times lately. I've also missed the start of my yoga class more than once because I get stuck checking the mirror. 

And I guess socially, I've stepped out of a few casual photos at my book club and some community events. I just... I didn't want to have to worry about how my face would look in the pictures.
Have you noticed yourself becoming more concerned about other aspects of your appearance, beyond just the skin on your cheeks and jaw?
No, not really. It's just my cheeks and jawline that I'm focused on. I haven't really noticed or been worried about anything else. It's just that one specific area since we changed the lighting.
Can you describe how you feel when you look in the mirror and notice your cheeks and jawline? Does it bring up feelings of anxiety, sadness, or something else entirely?

I don't know if I'd call it sadness. It's mostly just... frustration, I guess. 

I look in the mirror and see it, and I just feel annoyed that my skin looks so uneven and saggy now. And then, yeah, maybe a little bit of anxiety kicks in because I feel like I need to fix it or figure out how to cover it up before I head into the office, which is why I end up running late. But it's not some overwhelming sadness or anything like that. It just... it really bothers me.

When you notice your cheeks and jawline in the mirror, do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly — like adjusting your face, applying makeup a certain way, or taking extra time to check your appearance — to try to fix or feel better about what you're seeing?

Yeah, I definitely do some of those things. Most mornings, I end up checking my face from a few different angles in the mirror. And then I usually put on a little extra makeup to try and cover up the unevenness before I leave for the courthouse. 

I also catch myself comparing my face to the other women I see at work, just trying to see if their skin looks like mine. And like I mentioned before, if I'm really not feeling okay about how it looks, I'll just avoid being in any casual pictures.
Can you tell me if these feelings about your cheeks and jawline have been happening every day, or if they come and go?

It's pretty much every day. I mean, I have to get ready for work every morning, so I'm always looking in the mirror and seeing it. I don't really get a break from it. Some days are a little less frustrating if I feel like the makeup actually did a good job, but the feeling is still there every day.
Would you say that your concern about the appearance of your cheeks and jawline feels excessive or interferes with your overall sense of well-being?

I wouldn't say it's completely ruining my life or anything, but it does get in the way. I still get all my work done at the firm, but like I said, the extra time I spend checking the mirror and doing my makeup has made me rush into the courthouse late a few mornings. 

It also messes with my schedule outside of work. I've missed the start of my yoga class more than once because I was taking too long getting ready. And I've definitely skipped out on being in a few casual photos at my book club and other community events because I just didn't want to stress about how my face was going to look. So, yeah, it definitely interferes a bit.
Would you say that your concern about your cheeks and jawline is focused on a specific flaw that you believe is significant, even if others might not notice it?

Yes, exactly. It really started bothering me after we put a brighter mirror in our bathroom. Every time I look in it, I just see the skin around my cheeks and jaw looking uneven, or kind of saggy. It feels really obvious to me. But when I point it out to my husband, he says he doesn't really see what I'm talking about. So I guess other people might not notice it as much, but to me, it's a big deal.
Do you think that the issue with your cheeks and jawline is something that other people might not notice, but it feels really significant to you?

Yeah, um, like I just mentioned, that's pretty much exactly how it is. My husband says he doesn't see it, so I know other people probably aren't noticing it either. But to me, when I look in the mirror, it just stands out so much. So, yeah, it feels very significant to me, even if no one else is paying attention to it.
